about: Every dimension the F/A-18C build uses, with its source (an id in references.json) and where in it. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts. Stations (FS) are inches aft of the fuselage datum, waterlines (WL) inches above it (WL 100 is the fuselage reference line), buttlines (BL) inches from the centreline, positive to starboard. Angles round the fuselage (theta) follow TM-101724 figure 3: looking aft, 0 is the bottom centreline, 180 the top, 90 starboard and 270 port. A fact taken from the old model, as a last resort, names the old model as its source and says why no other source had it; a detail copied from it under the fair-use policy is listed in its manifest entry (air-fa18c.md #2).

waterline.note: the fuselage reference line corresponds to WL 100.0 on the airplane

buttline.note: BL 0 is the centreline; BL grows to starboard (Y is right of the c.g.)

apex.note: the fuselage reference line (WL 100) is drawn through the nose apex and on aft past the stabilator; tp209033 figure 2 points WL 100 at the stabilator

chord.note: mean aerodynamic chord, projected; tp209033 and hatp give 11.52 ft (138.24 in) as the reference chord

root.note: NACA 65A with a sharp leading edge, at wing station 56.876 (cr201687 table 1: modified NACA 65A, 5.0%)

areas.note: totals for both sides. cr3608's 1/10-scale model gives 0.19, 0.55 and 0.62 ft2, which scale to 19, 55 and 62. The flaps' 48.4 is not built: their fronts stand on the hinge line the photos show (layout.hinge), which makes them 55.5

toe.note: toe out, as the model table gives it

airfoils.note: NACA 65A basic thickness forms: half-thickness y at chordwise station x, both in percent of chord. Another thickness takes y/t interpolated linearly in t between the tabulated forms (TR-84's own method, by its cross plots); above 5% the 5% ratios hold, which TR-84's 63-series cross plots show moving under 2% between 5% and 6%.

layout.about: Placements no source states, fitted to the NASA three-views with the published planforms (views.py's masks, the side view anchored at the apex on WL 100). Each says what it was fitted to. Provisional until the reference airframe's photos confirm them.

wing.where: figure 5, PDF page 31 (traced by views.py), with hatp figure 2's side view for the keel. The anhedral: photos.py's cameras and tips.py (rotating the wing about the junction; deflections fitted, or held at rest in flight) over the ground photo dvids9820799 and the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145, their cameras solved with the rest (fin tips within 0.3 in)
wing.note: the wing's chord plane at the LEX-wing junction (BL 54.5, FS 404.05): the FS 357 section's LEX tip stands 31 in above its keel, and the keel is at WL 82.5. The anhedral is the photos', the jet parked (the user's choice, 2026-10-30): cr201687's -3 deg (wing.dihedral) leaves the tips' trailing corners about 5 in low in the ground photo (+-2 in or more: its flaps and ailerons droop) and 10 in low in three in-flight photos (8.7-10.3 leaving each out), the difference the wing bending up at 1 g (task: wing flex). Rotating the wing about the junction fits the flight photos a little better than raising it, and the junction itself measures no higher (4 in lower, +-2.3, two photos). The HATP front view draws the outer wing about 10 in higher

flex.unit: BL in, where the bend starts; in, the wingtip's rise at 1 g of lift; [BL in, share of the tip's rise]
flex.where: the rise: tm212871 printed page 17 and figure 12(a), FDMS target 12 (span station 193.8, figure 5) about 1.4 in, and 1.7 in after a roll, in steady level flight against ground rest, taken to the tip by the ground test's shape; the shape: tm210726 figure 16, load case D3, the forward box's measured deflection (1.1, 1.8, 3.1, 5.1, 6.2 and 10.0 in at the stations, 13.6 in at span station 222.1), read off the figure
flex.note: the wing bent up by lift (task: wing flex), as the shape key flex and the bend joints flex_* driven by the load factor of the lift (the drive load: 0 parked, 1 in level flight). Both reports fly the Active Aeroelastic Wing jet, whose wing has the preproduction torsional stiffness, a little softer than a production C's; its targets outboard of the fold carry the fold's free play. The bend starts at the LEX-wing junction (layout.wing's buttline) and takes a cantilever's shape, lift along the span as the chord and stiffness as the chord times the section's depth squared, streamwise sections rigid: outboard of BL 150 it follows the ground test's shape within 0.015 of the tip's rise, inboard it bends 0.05-0.06 less (the test's load and the fuselage's restraint are not flight's). The photo match agrees within its uncertainty: posed at 1 g with the in-flight photos, the wingtips' trailing corners fit best near a 3.5 in rise and the parked photos' wing and fin edges best with none

stabilator.where: figure 2, top view; natops 1.1.2 for the length; the waterline from the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145 (tips.py, deflections held at rest, the cameras photos.py solved)
stabilator.note: the root leading edge of the exposed panel (BL 41.6: the 21.6 ft span less the 14.67 ft exposed span). The views from straight above and below (dvids7487365, 7487366, 9820744), each photo's left and right sides averaged to cancel its camera's registration, read the leading edge 0.1 in and the trailing edge 0.05 in from the model's here (sky check); moving the panel 1.8 or 2.9 in aft took them to -0.6 and +1.5, or -0.9 and +2.5. It was first placed for the 56 ft overall length with an 8 in corner round; with the photos' 13 in round (layout.stabilator_corner) the tips' aftmost point falls at FS 729.8, 2.9 in short of it, and the photos' own apex and aftmost point give 55.84 ft (overall.length). WL 106.8: the in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners 6.8 in above where cr3608 figure 3's and tp209033 figure 2's WL 100 had them (6.3-7.7 leaving each photo out; 4-7.5 with trim free), the root then 3.8 in above the engine axes (layout.nozzle, WL 103); the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published

stabilator_corner.where: the sky check's photo edge places round each stabilator's trailing tip corner, cast onto the posed panel's plane, fitted as the cited tip line and trailing edge joined by a circle tangent to both, the panel's offset free (each photo's registration): 13.25 and 13.25 in (dvids7487365 left and right), 12.0 and 12.25 (dvids9820744), 13.0 and 13.0 (dvids7487366), 12.25 (dvids7487368 right), fitting to 0.13-0.19 in rms (0.52 for the last). The model's own outline through the same fit reads 7.5-8.0 for its 8. Variants with the panel unmoved: the corner's sky check, each photo's sides averaged, read +2.76 in with 8 in and +0.51 with 13 in, the leading and trailing edges unchanged (+0.10, +0.05). HATP figure 2's top view, a small drawing, cuts the corner back about 11 in along the tip, where a 13 in round leaves the tip line visibly (by 0.5 in) about 17 in from the corner
stabilator_corner.note: the radius of the round on each stabilator tip's trailing corner, tangent to the tip and to the trailing edge, 20.5 in from the corner along each; it takes 1.3 ft2 off the 88.0 for both sides (stabilator.area). cr201687's planform, which the build keeps everywhere else, is the theoretical one with sharp corners. Judged by where the traced tip seemed to leave its line it was first put at 8 in: a 13 in circle stays within 0.5 in of its tangent for 3.6 in past the tangent point. The leading corner reads sharp and the leading edge straight within a few degrees of the cited sweep. The corner landmarks stay where the edges' lines meet, as the photos are marked

fin.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): the fin tips' four corners in 6-9 photos (+-1.8 in along, +-0.3 in across); moved 1.5 in forward (2026-10-31): the fin tips' leading corners in 15-16 photos stand 2.0 in forward of the earlier build (+-2.2) and the trailing corners 2.9 in (+-2.4), and the sky check (verify/skyline.py) reads the leading edge 0.6-1.0 in inside the photos' all along it (FS 528-624, 10-14 photos each), about 1.0 in of stations at its sweep: the move lies between the two; moved 1.0 in further forward (2026-11-02): the tips' leading corners in 16-17 photos stood 1.0 in forward of the build (+-1.3) and the trailing corners 2.0 in (+-1.4), the leading edges traced in 13 photos and cast onto each fin's own plane 1.2 in forward all along their height on both fins (no sweep the photos agree on: single photos tilt both ways), and the sky check read the leading edge 0.4 in inside and the aft end 1.0 in outside
fin.note: leading edge at root and tip, on cr201687's planform, sweep and cant: the photos put the tips 8 in further aft and 7 in further outboard than the HATP views were fitted to give (FS 613.6, BL 71.4), the HATP side view's own top trailing corner standing 8.8 in aft of the old fit too; the root lies 95 in down the 20 deg cant from the tip (BL 38.9, on the nacelle's shoulder)

hinge.where: dvids7487365 (straight below, sharp, against clear sky): one straight line, with the hinge fittings and actuator fairings on it, runs along the lower surface of both wings across the flap and the aileron; traced at 16 points (BL 57-225 right, 57-211 left), cast onto the posed wing, it lies at 0.704-0.720 of the chord, rising inboard; the value is the median of the 11 points along the flaps. The aileron's front, which cr201687's aileron area sets (wing.areas, 0.699), stands 0.3-1.0 in ahead of it on both wings; cr201687's flap area would have put the flap's front 4.6-5.0 in behind it
hinge.note: the lower surface's hinge line of the trailing-edge flap and the aileron, as a share of the wing's chord from the leading edge. The flaps' fronts are built on it, which makes them 55.5 ft2 for both sides, where cr201687 table 1 gives 48.4 and cr3608's 1/10-scale model 62; the flaps' area is not built. The traced line is a photo match edge (dvids7487365 hinge_*), which the old flap missed by 4.3-4.4 in. dvids9820744, softer, read the same line 1.2-5.0 in ahead of the old flap front and 3.1-4.2 in behind the aileron's: both now about 3 in off it the same way, its camera's registration

surfaces.unit: BL in; the rudder as fractions of the fin's span from its root
surfaces.where: figure 2 (control surfaces labelled in the top and side views); the flap's outer end and the aileron's inner end by photo match, with tm210726 figure 6
surfaces.note: spans of the hinged surfaces: the leading-edge flaps split at the fold (tp209033 PDF page 17) and run from the LEX-wing junction to the tip; the flap's inner end and the rudder's are read off figure 2's sketch. The flap's outer trailing corner is the photo match's fold_trailing point (BL 152.8 +- 0.8, six marks in five photos), 7 in inboard of the sketch's 160; the gap to the aileron is 3.1 in wide at the trailing edge in dvids9820744. tm210726 figure 6 (to scale within 1%: its two references and the tip agree) draws the load zones on the flap ending at BL 154 and those on the aileron starting at 156. The aileron's inboard 6.5 in lies behind the fold line and folds with the outer panel. The aileron runs to the tip (the sketch drew it ending at BL 220): with it drooped in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788, sky shows directly outboard of its end, under the tip's launcher rail. Each surface's chord fraction follows from its cr201687 area over these spans

gear.unit: FS in for the axle centres; WL in for the axles; in for the track (between the main wheels' centres) and the nose wheels' spacing
gear.where: NATOPS 1.1.2's heights for the axles; verify/photos.py over photos.json for the track and the nose wheels' spacing (the wheels' hub faces in 6-9 photos, +-0.4 in across); tp209033 figure 2 for the stations, which the photos confirm (FS 495.1 and 280.9, +-1.2)
gear.note: the wheel centres' stations from the nose apex on tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82 marked) at its 56 ft scale, wheelbase 17.77 ft. The axles' heights are set so NATOPS's static heights hold over the ground beneath the tyres (fins 15 ft 3 in, canopy 10 ft 6 in): the jet then sits 0.9 deg nose down. The photos' taxiing jets put the main axle 2.9 in higher (WL 44.3 +-1.5) and the nose axle 0.8 in higher (45.6 +-0.9), more nose down, as a lighter or moving jet may sit. The track is the photos': the main hub faces stand 66.2 in either side, less a third of each tyre's width to its centre (tp209033's rear view drew the track 116 in). The nose wheels' spacing is dvids8559777's, head-on: both tyres cast onto the axle's station plane from its solved camera stand at BL +8.6 and -8.2, each 6.4-6.5 in wide against the 6.6 in read off the close-ups, so the cast's scale holds; a steered pair would read narrower, not wider. The photo match agrees within its spread (the hub faces at BL 10.3-11.3, about 2 in further out than the 8.9 an earlier solve gave, when one photo's mark on a far wheel's inboard face pulled its camera to 16 px). Tyre diameters from dvids9820808's matched camera; widths read off the gear close-ups dvids8678626 and dvids8678628 against those diameters

canopy.unit: FS in, WL in; the sill as [FS, WL, BL]; top, the canopy's top line behind the crown as [FS, WL]; glass, the exponents of the superellipse the glass's section follows from the sill to the top centreline, at the bow's foot and at the aft corner (linear between); screen, the windscreen's frame sill as [FS, WL, BL] ahead of the bow's foot; screen_glass, [FS, exponent]: the windscreen glass's superellipse exponent, held to that station and rising linearly to glass's first at the bow's foot; joint, [FS, WL, BL] along the joint where the canopy's aft fairing meets the spine, from its top down to the sill; glass_edge, [FS, WL] readings along the glass's lower edge on the left, where the metal panel below it meets it
canopy.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): windscreen_base in 5 photos, bow_top 2, canopy_aft 3, bow_foot 4, sill_aft 4 (+-1 in); canopy_crown and the sill's middle in dvids9820808 alone. The sill's buttlines from the 22-photo solve (2026-11-02): bow_foot BL 15.24 in 8 photos and sill_aft 20.15 in 7 (+-0.4), each 1.3-1.6 in further out than the first solve put them, which every single photo left out keeps (1.06-1.81); the middle, which only dvids9820808 sees, moved out by their mean. TM 101724's cited sections (FS 184-253) agree: they stand 2-2.5 in wider than the earlier sill. glass and top: the canopy outlines traced in the seven photos with well-solved cameras, split fore and aft by the station of the model's silhouette nearest each traced point, the cameras held while only the canopy changes. The glass's upper edge against the sky in the profiles dvids9820808 and dvids9820801 (the strongest step in each pixel column, cast onto the centreline) gives the top line behind the crown; the two agree within 0.15 in (0.45 at FS 264), three readings that caught the cockpit inside left out. With that top line the outlines' median miss is 0.28 in (1.00 with the cited sections unchanged): forward of FS 280 any exponent from 1.8 to 2.3 does as well, aft 1.0 and 1.2 do (0.20 and 0.25 in) while 1.6 and 2.0 miss by 0.55 and 0.83 screen: the windscreen frame's sill line traced in the side photos (layout.panels, sill_line_right), sampled. screen_glass (2026-11-02): with the windscreen's section above it drawn in to a superellipse, the quarter views' sky outline just behind the front base (FS 192-216, BL 8-13) read +1.18 in with an exponent of 2.0, +1.25 with 1.6, +0.69 with 1.3 and +0.47 with 1.1 (where the head-up display's glass then pokes through); 1.3 held back to the bow drew the glass at FS 216-240 0.77 in inside, so it rises to the canopy's 2.0 at the bow's foot from FS 200: +0.82 there over 7 photos (was +1.22), the glass at FS 216-240 -0.01 over 9, dvids9820748's traced windscreen edge 0.19 in (was 1.04) joint (2026-11-03): the seam behind the canopy's aft fairing traced in dvids9820801 (right) and triangulated against its mirror image traced in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788 (left): the two left photos agree within 0.3 in, each pixel 0.0-0.4 px off the traced line; the point at the top (BL 11.3) missed by 3-6 px and is left out. Cast onto the skin instead, the right photo put the joint at FS 333-334 and the left at 338-339 over a spine faded too long behind the canopy (2 in low there) glass_edge (2026-11-04): the glass's lower edge, its dark seal line found column by column in dvids9820782 (FS 254-317) and dvids9820788 (FS 280-315) and cast onto the canopy's skin: the two agree within 0.5 in where both see it. It runs 3.5 in above the sill at FS 254 and rises steadily to WL 151.5 at FS 317, a broad metal panel below it, ahead of the canopy's aft end tail (2026-11-05): the top's height above the spine's crown at the canopy's aft end, the sky check over the 31 photos solved together: the top's centreline reads WL 152.30 at FS 324-328 (8 side photos, 151.53-152.80), 152.09 at FS 328-332 (5) and 152.35 at FS 332-336 (3), against the crown's 152.35, the spine running flat to the canopy's aft frame in the profiles where the old model's hood rose 1.8 in; the canopy's top falls to it at the aft end and the spine runs on flat behind, where the old model's hood rose 1.8 in. The canopy_aft marks triangulate 1.2 in below the old model's height there (6 photos). The canopy's aft part is the section the photos traced (the user's decision, 2026-11-05): the old model's (laid 2026-11-04) stood 2-2.7 in outside the head-on photos' outline beside it, where the traced section comes within 0.5 in
canopy.note: the windscreen's front base, the bow between windscreen and canopy, the canopy's crown and aft end on the centreline, and the canopy's sill from the bow's foot to the canopy's aft lower corner. The cited sections between FS 184 and 253 leave the skin 2-2.5 in wider than the sill, so the build draws the glass in to meet it

eye.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json: dvids9820808's helmet located from its camera solved with the other 11 photos, centre FS 254.5 WL 154.4, top WL 159.3
eye.note: the design eye, provisional: a little ahead of and below the helmet's centre in the reference photo, where the pilot sits reaching for the canopy bow

hardpoints.where: figure 4-4 (External Stores Limitations): each station's distance from the centreline, 19.5 ft (stations 1 and 9), 11.2 (2 and 8), 7.3 (3 and 7) and 3.7 (4 and 6), to a tenth of a foot
hardpoints.note: stations 1-9 (air-stores.md). A station's buttline is the figure's distance, where its store hangs. The wing stations' mounts sit on the wing's lower surface at that buttline and the chord fraction given, the store straight below; the tip stations' on the wingtip (the build places them there, not at the buttline), whose launcher carries the round out to the figure's line; the fuselage stations' on the skin straight below their station and buttline, the cheek stations' inboard of their rounds (station 6). The stations along the length and the chord fraction are provisional until step 5 matches the stores themselves. The flight model's store positions (fa18c.go) are its own estimates, not this figure: its outboard pylons at 3.35 m (131.9 in) and its cheek stations at 0.55 m (21.7 in), 'a plausible figure, not a survey'. The photos' Litening pod hangs on the centreline at FS 350-445 (dvids7487365, dvids9820744 and dvids8901347 agree), forward of station 5: its adapter, not the station, places it

stations.where: NATOPS figure 4-4 hangs the round 3.7 ft (44.4 in) out, and dvids7487365 (from below) agrees: its right-cheek AIM-120's nose and tail, cast from the solved camera, put the axis at FS 420-567 (the round's 144 in) and BL 46.8 at WL 70, less 0.24 in for each inch higher, so BL 44.4 at WL 80. The round's inboard side clears the nacelle (BL 38.2 at WL 80, 42.4 at WL 84, at FS 496) only below WL 82, so it hangs against the nacelle's lower outboard corner with its axis about WL 80. The mount is the skin straight above its inboard side, BL 41.5, which the build drapes to WL 85.8; the station is the round's middle

strips.unit: [FS, WL, BL] in, each strip's ends on the right, mirrored on the left; width: in, across each strip
strips.where: the ends' middles marked in the solved photos and triangulated (layout.lights where): the fins' strips from 16 and 18 rays over 90 deg, within 0.2-2.1 in; the nacelles' from 7 and 9 over 90 deg; the tip launchers' from the four ground photos (4 rays over 76 deg), the strip under the rail from 2 rays over 31 deg
strips.note: the formation light strips other than the nose's (layout.formation), flush with what they stand on. Their width is not measured: the nose strip's 1.7 in. The tip launchers' strips stand on the launchers, which are stores (step 5): the build places the fins' and the nacelles'

lights.where: natops 2.6.1 names the lights (position, formation, strobe, approach, landing, hook and probe). Their places (2026-11-06): marked by a helper in 35 solved photos and triangulated through the bundle's cameras, each light from 2-33 rays over 31-90 deg, the rays within 0.1-2.6 in of each point: the position lights' lenses on each LEX's edge aft-below the fence (19 rays) and at the forward tip of the fairing under each wing's fold (5); the white one closing the aft end of the right fin's upper tip pod (the left's ends in an opaque cap, 7); the strobes' red lenses on the fins' outboard faces below the tip pods (33); the formation strips' middles, on the fins' outboard faces (16 and 18 rays at their ends), on the nacelles' sides between the flap and the stabilator (7 and 9), and on the tip launchers above and below the rail (the wing bends in flight: from the four ground photos only, 4 rays; below the rail 2 rays over 31 deg); the landing light and the amber middle lens of the approach lights' stack on the nose gear's strut, gear down (8 and 10 rays; dvids7418477 puts both 1.7 in lower, its strut compressed otherwise). The hook and probe lights are natops's, provisional
lights.note: points: [FS, WL, BL] in; a light on a gear part gives it as the gear stands down and names the part, the points file giving it at rest on that part. strips (layout.strips) carries the formation strips' ends

The closed exit's radius is the gas path's, at the divergent flaps' faces, which the build stands 1.5 in inside the outer flaps (no source gives their thickness): closing turns each flap about its hinge until that face reaches it, the outer lip then about 10.8 in from the axis, as dvids7070877 (from behind, both nozzles closed) shows it, about 10-11 in. tm100159's R9 is GE's spec deck's, the measured jet 5-10% wider (its page 8), and a running jet on the ground at intermediate holds a wider throat (264 in2, tm4538), so a closed nozzle seen low down stands a little more open. The parked photos show the nozzles open; the HARV (tm101724's jet) had its outer flaps removed. The divergent flaps' length is the eye's (no source gives it), and so are the stepped tabs: each outer flap's aft part steps round by a quarter of its width about a third of its length from the exit, so the seams between flaps make a staircase
